newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt officials on EU tour before trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt officials on EU tour before trade deal.

text.p: Egypt's minister of trade and its chief trade negotiator will tour European nations to solicit support for their case in talks on a planned trade partnership agreement with the 15-nation European Union, an official said on Sunday.

Ambassador Gamal Bayyoumi told Reuters that he would accompany Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily on Monday for talks with officials in France, Spain, Germany and the Netherlands as Egypt edged close to the deal that provides for free trade in services and manufactured goods.
"We realise that we are dealing with more than one country and that there are some countries that are sensitive about one issue -- we're going to explain our position," Bayyoumi said.
"We are not considering not signing the agreement but we evaluate it regularly to find its opportunities and challenges and how to end up with the best deal," he added.
Egypt is pressing for easier access to European Union markets for Egyptian foodstuffs, especially rice, potatoes and processed foodstuffs.

The EU, hamstrung by the Common Agricultural Policy, has previously argued for quotas that reflect the historical level of Egyptian exports. Egypt says these are based on a time when it traded mainly with the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe.

"What they are talking about is what I call doubling the zero. They are talking about quotas which were set in 1977 which were next to nothing and if you double nothing you get more nothing," Bayyoumi said.

According to a remarks by an unnamed trade official published in the government-run press last week, the European Union had offered import quotas of 300,000 tonnes for rice, 17,000 tonnes of oranges and 500,000 tonnes of cut flowers.

Bayyoumi, who held talks with EU officials in Brussels earlier this month, did not confirm the quotas but said the 15-nation bloc wanted 300 percent tariffs on rice, oranges and up to 500 percent tariffs on processed foods like jam and biscuits, which constitute one-fifth of industrial exports.

"I am optimistic, but reservedly so. Both parties are moving but we're still shouting not enough at each other. They are beginning to put zeros to the right but not enought zeros for us," said Bayyoumi, who is also assistant foreign minister.
This month, Spain said it would lobby Egypt's case at the EU and Bayyoumi said he was also looking to Italy for help.
"They (Spain and Italy) are Mediterranean countries and they are also Europeans. We're seeking support," he said.
Bayyoumi had said earlier this month that Egypt and the European Union were working towards reaching an agreement by the time Mediterranean states meet in Malta in April to discuss cooperation.
